scope_limit_disclaimer: SOUND HEADLINE = structural arms only (count / dependency / negation vs the independent tsc oracle). The relation arm is MEASURED, not guaranteed (no direction oracle: admitRelation has no way to reject a reversed edge, so both falseAdmit and recallTrue print 100% by construction). Semantic slots (invariant / sideeffect / advisory prose) tsc cannot witness are NOT covered here at all.
limits: recall over PLANTED mutations on a synthetic-labelled fixture, not recall over arbitrary real-world facts
covers only the 4 oracle-bearing shapes (count, relation, dependency, negation); advisory/predicate prose has no sound oracle and is out of scope

recall is INDEX-BUILD-DEPENDENT by roughly an order of magnitude (count/dependency recall 4.29% dist-absent vs 100% dist-form; negation recall 4.25% vs 35.67%) — a bare percentage without the build recipe is not a citable number

on the dist-form (intended/operating) index at git sha 9eb4d7f, the shipped door is NOT 0-false-admit for dependency (309/23702=1.30%, 2 of them call-eligible) or count (9/163=5.52%) — this is a genuine measured finding, not a framing choice, and it contradicts the 0-FP claim in docs/design/95-benchmark-methodology.md for these two arms at this build+rev; negation remains 0-false-admit in both build states measured
relation's 100%/100% is a construction artifact of admitRelation having no direction oracle, not evidence of either soundness or unsoundness
this report measures ONE git sha (9eb4d7f) and TWO index builds; it does not sweep git history or other index tools
what_the_brief_got_wrong: the brief characterized bench-scorer's independence rule and per-arm two-co-primary output correctly; that part is accurate as described

the brief implied the test 'currently only console.log's these' numbers and asked for the smallest capture change — true; I did NOT edit the shipped test file. I added two throwaway, uncommitted test files under packages/adapter-io/test/_tmp-*.test.ts that reimplement the SAME accumulation bench-scorer.ts already does (to get raw numerators/denominators the console.log line omits), ran them, captured stdout, then deleted them before commit. Zero diff to the shipped instrument.

the brief's framing implied the dist-form vs dist-absent question was primarily about RECALL swinging (per the doc's L79-102 example). That is true, but this run surfaced a SECOND, more serious effect the brief did not anticipate: on the dist-form (operating) index at the CURRENT git sha, the door is no longer 0-false-admit for dependency and count — a genuine soundness regression/finding relative to the doc's claims, not just a recall swing. This is the most important single fact in this report and the brief's 'the trap is only about recall' framing undersold it.

the fixture pin's `substrate.rev` field says `e35dcce`, an OLDER commit than this worktree's HEAD (9eb4d7f). The pin's own comment clarifies the tsc oracle is 'a deterministic pure function of the checked-out src at this rev' (i.e. whatever is checked out, not the pinned annotation), and nothing in AC-7 enforces that the checked-out src matches `e35dcce` — only the SYNTHETIC self-proof fixture bytes (semantic-bench-fixture.json) are hash-pinned, not the substrate. So the numbers in this report are for 9eb4d7f, not e35dcce, and that drift is exactly why the doc's committed AC-6 comments (e.g. 'dependency = 0.08% residual...17/23577') no longer match this run (18/23702, 309/23702) — the population grew and, on dist-form, the dependency soundness invariant itself broke. This is worth flagging to the code owner, not something I fixed (out of scope for a measurement WP).
